A silent station corridor, every panel dead, ribbed bulkheads furred with frost, a tangle of severed cables drifting lazily across the passage, a hatch hanging half-open on a darkness beyond.
A ghostly command bridge, consoles dark and dusted, the captain's chair turned away and empty, a cracked main viewport framing a slow-wheeling starfield, nothing humming, nothing alive.
A vast wrecked hangar bay, a broken shuttle nose-down across the deck, one wing sheared clean, a single helmet drifting in the still air, the great bay doors frozen permanently half-shut.
A cold reactor chamber, the core dead and rimed with frost, coolant lines split and empty, warning plaques dangling from one bolt each, the whole space utterly silent and lightless.

A cargo hold packed with frozen containers, several drifting free of their moorings, frost crystals suspended mid-air like permanent snow, a crushed loader tilted against the far bulkhead, everything still.
A crashed wreck half-buried in grey asteroid regolith, one engine nacelle sheared off and lying fifty meters away, the hull buckled and open to vacuum, dust settled undisturbed across every surface.

An engineering deck choked with loose cabling, thick bundles hanging from every overhead bracket, pooling on the deck grating, conduits burst and empty, the machinery beneath cold and seized for years.

A medical bay with four empty gurneys drifting inches off the deck, restraint straps trailing, instrument arms locked in their last positions, every screen black, a single med-kit floating open and gutted.
An observation dome cracked open to space, the transparent panels spiderwebbed and one section missing entirely, stars visible through the gap, loose insulation drifting out slowly into the void.
A spiral stairwell frozen in zero gravity, every rung coated in frost, a clipboard and a boot suspended mid-shaft where someone left them long ago, the shaft vanishing into darkness above and below.
A docking ring, a derelict shuttle still berthed and clamped hard, its airlock hanging open, umbilical lines frozen stiff and cracked, both vessels dead and cold, no lights anywhere along the ring.

The exterior of a cruiser snapped cleanly in two, both halves drifting slowly apart, wiring and conduit spilling between them like entrails, hull plating peeled back, the interior cross-section open to hard vacuum.
A narrow escape-pod bay, every pod long gone, the ejection cradles empty and frost-coated, status lights dead, a single sealed suit locker standing open and stripped, the bay utterly silent.

A broad officers' mess, tables and benches bolted down but trays and utensils floating at varying heights, frost on every surface, a viewport showing only dark asteroid field, no warmth ever coming back.

The tight interior of a destroyed gun turret, the twin barrels jammed at full elevation, the gunner's seat cracked and empty, targeting screens shattered, shrapnel embedded in every wall of the tiny space.
A communications array room, every antenna control station dead, a wall of dark screens, cabling ripped from their housings, a slow rotation of torn paper readouts drifting in the cold still air.

An exterior view of a dead station, its ring section bent thirty degrees out of true, docking arms broken to stumps, solar panels shattered to bare struts, no running lights, no heat signature anywhere.

A cramped crew bunk corridor, locker doors hanging ajar, a few items of clothing frozen stiff and drifting in the passage, the overhead strip lights dark, every bunk behind each curtain cold and empty.

A ruined engine room at the stern of a derelict, the main drives dead and cold, thruster bells dark, hull plates around them warped by some long-past catastrophe, frost coating every seized component.

A long-dead hydroponics bay, the growing trays bone-dry and cracked, dead root systems brittle and brown, the overhead lighting rigs cold, irrigation lines shriveled, the whole bay a silent grey ruin of dead plants.
A tight airlock chamber, both inner and outer doors stuck open, the mechanism seized, frost thick on every surface, a single glove drifting in the middle of the small space, going nowhere.
An exterior close view of the hull, a great impact scar running forty meters across the plating, metal peeled outward in frozen petals, a dark void beyond where something once was, cold and still.

A security station at a corridor junction, blast shutters lowered on two passages, the guard console dark, a restraint cuff clipped to the desk rail, monitors dead, the chair pushed back and abandoned.

A vast empty fuel processing chamber, enormous tanks ruptured and dry, catwalks around them buckled and in places missing entirely, every gauge needle resting on zero, the air long gone, silence total and permanent.

A cold reactor chamber, the massive core dead and rimed with frost, coolant lines burst and frozen mid-drip, warning lights black, the surrounding catwalks sagging where support struts have buckled and let go.
